title: SDK journey-map standup notes — quickstarts & sample app alignment
content:
Standup: SDK journey-map + quickstarts alignment
Date: 2026-04-07
Facilitator: Nadia Patel
Attendees: Nadia, Liam, Mateo, Priya, Alicia, Jordan (partial)
Duration: 35m (ran over)
Location: zoom / #devexp thread

Purpose
- Sync on updated "journey map" for new users following a quickstart -> sample app -> deployment path.
- Decide ownership and immediate next actions for Quickstarts v2 and the 'todo-lite' sample app.

High level takeaways
- We have 3 primary user flows to support: quick PoC (hosted API), prototype on Dedicated, and Private/VPC evaluation. The journey map needs branching for those.
- Quickstarts v2 draft is in GH (PR 409) but missing: telemetry hooks, one-click deploy for Dedicated, and a short troubleshooting section.
- 'todo-lite' sample app (React + Python backend) shows the API call pattern we want to recommend, but it currently uses synchronous token streaming that blows up cost in the example (needs batching demo).

Notes / Discussion (rough)
- Mateo: walked through user path A (hosted API). Highlights: make the initial steps zero-config, show how to set API key, then run a single sample call. The current README is too long — propose a 4-step quickstart card on top.
- Priya: telemetry must be plumbed into the sample apps so we can auto-collect latency + token count. Suggested events: quickstart_started, sample_run_complete, model_variant_selected, error_rate. Need to keep privacy — no PII or prompt text in telemetry.
- Liam: Dedicated one-click deploy needs a lightweight manifest generator (YAML) that maps to Dedicated stacks. Can we reuse release-engineering pipeline snippets? Action: Liam to draft manifest template.
- Alicia: Developer console screenshots are out-of-date; ask Console team for updated assets. Also: add a screenshot note about 'pin model version' for reproducibility.
- Jordan: flagged that the Python example uses naive loop to call generate per message; propose using the SDK.batch_messages helper (exists in alpha).

Decision log (quick)
- Keep repo structure: /quickstarts (1-file recipes) and /samples (full apps) — decision: YES. Rationale: low-friction + deep dive.
- Add telemetry stubs to every sample by default: minimal events + opt-out via env var. Decision: include telemetry, ensure privacy-preserving.
- Prioritize a 'cost-aware' section in quickstarts that explicitly shows batching, caching and approximate token cost with examples. Decision: top-3 priority for v2.

Action items (owner / due)
- Nadia: Draft quickstart landing card copy (4 steps + cost note) — due 2026-04-12.
- Liam O'Connor: Prototype Dedicated manifest generator & PR to scripts repo — due 2026-04-14.
- Mateo Rivera: Trim README for hosted quickstart, add 4-step badge and embed minimal example call — due 2026-04-09.
- Priya Singh: Create telemetry event schema + small privacy checklist; post to Confluence and add to PR checklist — due 2026-04-10.
- Alicia Chen: Request updated Console screenshots and export assets; add to assets folder — due 2026-04-11.
- Jordan Blake: Replace naive per-message loop with SDK.batch_messages in todo-lite sample and include before/after cost numbers — due 2026-04-13.
- All: Review PR 409 and comment with checklist items (telemetry, screenshots, cost section) — target 2026-04-10.

Blockers / Risks
- Telemetry schema not finalized — blocks adding telemetry stubs to samples. Mitigation: add opt-out flag and placeholder events for now.
- Dedicated manifest format may change based on infra team's review — risk of rework. Keep manifest minimal.
- Console screenshot availability might delay the landing card. Use temporary screenshots if not delivered.

Notes to self / rough TODOs (informal)
- Write a short blurb for the onboarding email: "Try our hosted quickstart — 5 mins to first response". Include cost note (example: ~0.8c per call) — need to verify tokens math.
- Collect 3 user personas to ensure journey branches: Side-project dev, platform engineer evaluating Dedicated, enterprise SRE evaluating Private.
- Consider a "cost calculator" demo link embedded in quickstarts that pre-fills typical params (seq len, tokens/response). Low priority.

Sample code excerpt (inline example to include in quickstart card)
- Python minimal example (one-liner style):
  from redwood_sdk import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
  print(client.generate("Summarize this doc in one sentence"))
- NOTE: in the sample app we'll show batching pattern, e.g. pseudo: client.batch_messages([messages]) to reduce per-token overhead.

Follow-ups for next standup (2026-04-14)
- Quickstart landing copy: review + finalize.
- PR 409: Ensure telemetry fields exist and screenshots are updated.
- Demo of todo-lite after Jordan's batching changes with before/after cost metrics.
- Short UX review with Console team (Alicia to schedule).

Misc / fragments captured from chat (raw)
- "If we show cost numbers, make them conservative and call out assumptions." — @mrivera
- "Beta SDK has batch_messages but it's not documented; we should mark as experimental in sample." — @liam
- "Can we put a tiny 'why this matters' card explaining batching & caching? Non-technical PMs love that." — @priya

Closing notes
- Good alignment overall. We need to move fast on telemetry + cost examples to make v2 feel trustworthy. Prioritize small, concrete wins we can ship in <2 weeks.

End of notes.
